meta.title: Trailmark — CLI bookmarking tool
meta.subtitle: Scoping
meta.headline: Let’s pin down the CLI before we build.
meta.lede: A handful of decisions shape the whole tool. Each is pre-set to a **recommended default** with the reasoning; review, override, and flag anything to discuss.

context.note: Trailmark saves, tags, and re-opens URLs from the terminal. Storage, sync, and the query language are the open questions.

items.desc: how you find a saved link again

questions.question: Where do bookmarks live?
questions.why: A single local file is the simplest thing that works offline and is trivial to back up; a DB is premature at this scale.

options.label: Embedded SQLite
options.detail: Scales to huge libraries; adds a dependency.

options.label: Cloud-backed from day one
options.detail: Needs accounts + network; conflicts with offline-first.

questions.question: Sync strategy?
questions.why: Punting sync to the user’s existing git/Dropbox keeps v1 tiny and avoids running any server.

options.label: Built-in sync server
options.detail: Most seamless; most to build and operate.

options.label: Bring-your-own folder (git/Dropbox)
options.detail: You already have it; we just write a file.

questions.question: Which search inputs should v1 support?
questions.why: Tag + full-text cover the two ways people actually recall a link; regex is power-user polish that can wait.
